extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners studying or evaluating creativity in large language models
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and applying a holistic, scalable evaluation framework to measure creativity of large language model (LLM) generations across multiple domains and dimensions (quality, novelty, diversity).

rubrics_metrics.name: CreativityPrism taxonomy — three dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A taxonomy of creativity that emphasizes three dimensions: quality, novelty, and diversity of LLM generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework consolidates tasks and metrics around these three dimensions to provide a holistic view of creativity; evaluations should explicitly report per-dimension scores rather than a single aggregate creativity number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domains to cover: divergent thinking, creative writing, logical reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidates eight tasks from three domains: divergent thinking, creative writing, and logical reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should span these domains (or clearly justify domain choices) because creativity manifests differently across them; use tasks representative of each domain to avoid domain-specific overfitting of metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple tasks (eight tasks) for holistic assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework consolidates eight tasks from the three domains into the taxonomy to assess creativity across different scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a diverse set of tasks rather than relying on a single benchmark or prompt type so that measured performance reflects breadth of creative ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability via automatic evaluation judges
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework is designed to be scalable with reliable automatic evaluation judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer automatic judges for speed and scalability, but ensure their reliability by validating them against human annotations; present validation evidence when reporting automated evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of automatic judges against human annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic evaluation judges used in the framework have been validated against human annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using automated metrics, demonstrate alignment with human judgments (e.g., correlation analyses, agreement measures) to support claims about creativity scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-dimensional/holistic reporting (avoid single-dimension conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A holistic, multi-dimensional framework is essential because high performance in one creative dimension or domain rarely generalizes to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and analyze per-dimension and per-domain results; be cautious in drawing broad claims from improvements on only one dimension because metrics (e.g., novelty) may correlate weakly or negatively with other dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat novelty as a distinct dimension with potentially weak correlations
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty metrics often show weak or negative correlations with other metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure novelty separately and interpret novel-high scores in the context of quality and diversity; investigate trade-offs between novelty and other dimensions rather than assuming positive co-variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking across model families (proprietary vs open-source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate a diverse set of models (the paper evaluates 17 state-of-the-art proprietary and open-sourced LLMs) to understand relative strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both proprietary and open-source models to reveal systematic differences (e.g., the paper finds proprietary LLMs lead in creative writing and logical reasoning by ~15% but not in divergent thinking); contextualize results by model class.
